body_markdown:
Emergent has gained attention in the AI app builder market with its multi-agent approach to application development. However, its credit-based pricing can make costs harder to predict during repeated building and debugging. For users seeking a different approach,[Floot](https://floot.com/) offers a full-stack app-building platform with managed infrastructure and an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) for supported AI assistants.


Other alternatives provide different approaches to application development, from visual no-code environments to AI-powered cloud IDEs. This guide examines eight Emergent alternatives based on pricing, backend infrastructure, mobile app capabilities, and ease of use, helping non-technical founders, freelancers, and small business owners find the right platform for their projects.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through existing AI assistants** : Floot's MCP connector supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, allowing users to create, edit, and publish full-stack applications through supported AI workflows.
- **Mobile app builds on every plan** :[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/en/mobile) are available on all Floot plans, with 2/month on Free, 12/month on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Google Play publishing requires a paid Floot plan.
- **Managed backend infrastructure** :[Floot's built-in infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) includes PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, transactional email, and hosting.
- **Daily building-action limits** : Floot's connector-driven building uses existing AI subscriptions rather than a separate Floot AI build-credit bill. Hosting usage and optional Floot AI features have separate allowances and charges.
- **Simplified application deployment** : Floot manages core infrastructure and supports web and mobile publishing workflows, while complex applications still require testing and app-store submissions remain subject to developer-account requirements and store approval.


## **Understanding AI App Builder Platforms**


AI app builders have transformed how non-technical founders bring ideas to life. These platforms use natural language prompts to generate working applications, but they differ significantly in their approach to AI billing, backend services, and deployment options.


When comparing AI app builders, consider their AI development workflows, database and authentication services, hosting and deployment options, code export policies, and pricing predictability.


Emergent uses a multi-agent workflow for interface development, backend integration, and automated testing. Its Standard plan costs $20/month when billed annually and includes 100 monthly credits, while Pro costs $200/month when billed annually and includes 750 monthly credits.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


Rather than requiring builders to learn a separate development environment, Floot lets users[build inside AI workflows](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) they already use.


### **Primary Focus**


- **MCP connector architecture** : Works with supported AI assistants, including Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor, using existing AI subscriptions for connector-driven code generation
- **Complete backend infrastructure** : Managed PostgreSQL, authentication with Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering, file storage, transactional email, payment integrations, and[background tasks](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , with recurring scheduled jobs available for published apps on paid plans
- **Mobile app conversion** : Every plan includes iOS and Android builds with 2/month on Free, 12/month on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power
- **Daily action limits** : Building actions reset daily (100/1,000/5,000 by tier) rather than depleting from a monthly pool
- **Drawing-based visual editing** : Use[preview annotations](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/editor-and-preview) to select elements, mark changes, and help the connected assistant make targeted edits


### **Why Floot Stands Out**


Floot serves non-technical founders building MVPs, small business owners creating custom internal tools, and freelancers serving clients who need both web and mobile applications. The platform supports use cases across employee scheduling, real estate transaction management, ecommerce workflows, and internal business tools.


A major advantage is the combination of AI-assisted development and managed application infrastructure. Floot provides the database, authentication, storage, hosting, and[payment integrations](https://floot.com/en/integrations) needed to turn an application idea into a working product with saved data and user accounts.


Connector-driven building uses existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions without a second Floot AI build-credit bill. Floot plan fees, hosting usage, and charges for optional AI-powered features are separate. This gives builders a way to manage application infrastructure without assembling multiple backend services themselves. Live Stripe payments and customer-facing email from a verified sending domain require a paid Floot plan. Stripe payments also require a connected Stripe account.


### **Organizational Fit**


- **Free** : Zero cost to start at $0/month, with 100 actions/day, 2 mobile builds/month, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting credit
- **Pro** :[$25/month](https://floot.com/en/pricing) with 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 AI credits/month, $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds/month, and custom domains
- **Power** : $100/month with 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 AI credits/month, $25/month hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds. Hosting usage beyond included allowances draws on prepaid hosting credit


The prices above are monthly billing rates in USD. Annual billing offers two months free. AI credits cover features such as in-app AI, image generation, and Floot's optional agent rather than ordinary connector-driven building.


Floot's connector gives authorized AI assistants tools for reading files, writing code, running SQL, testing, and deploying, while the assistant handles reasoning and code generation. Available actions depend on the connected client's permissions. Users retain ownership of their code and data on every plan, while downloading the complete project as a ZIP is available on paid plans.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable positions itself as a prompt-to-app platform with a guided beginner experience. It offers a dedicated development environment and an active community of builders who share tutorials, templates, and examples.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Guided onboarding** : Designed for first-time builders with structured workflows
- **GitHub integration** : Supports code export and version control through GitHub
- **Backend options** : Managed database services through Lovable Cloud or Supabase
- **Element-level editing** : Visual interface for modifying components
- **Active community** : Tutorials, templates, and examples for different application types


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable offers a dedicated app-building interface and also supports development through external AI assistants using its MCP server. Unlike Floot's connector-driven building model, Lovable's MCP actions that invoke its agent consume Lovable workspace credits. It focuses on web applications and offers backend services through Lovable Cloud or Supabase.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable's Pro plan starts at $25/month on monthly billing, with credit limits and optional top-ups that can increase costs during intensive development. The platform focuses on web applications and does not include native iOS and Android app conversion.


Lovable suits builders who want a standalone interface with community resources and do not require built-in native mobile app publishing.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI app builder that supports prototypes and full-stack applications, with Bolt Cloud providing managed databases, authentication, and hosting.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based execution** : No local setup required for building prototypes
- **Fast preview** : Quick iteration on frontend designs
- **Code access** : Direct file inspection and editing
- **Token-based billing** : Usage measured in tokens rather than credits


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new supports rapid frontend prototyping and demonstration builds. It can be used for validating concepts before expanding application functionality. The platform provides built-in backend capabilities through Bolt Cloud.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new uses token-based billing, with Pro starting at $25/month on monthly billing and higher allowances available through additional plan options. Bolt Cloud supports databases and authentication, while mobile projects can be developed through its Expo integration.


Bolt.new works well for builders who prioritize rapid visual prototyping and browser-based application development.


## **4. Base44**


Base44 was acquired by Wix in June 2025 and focuses on speed-oriented MVP development. It positions itself as a quick path to working prototypes with built-in backend services.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Speed-focused builds** : Optimized for rapid MVP creation
- **Built-in backend** : Database and authentication included
- **Credit-based pricing** : Monthly credit allowances for building
- **Wix ownership** : Acquired by Wix in June 2025


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 targets founders who need fast prototypes and want to build and publish applications quickly through its managed platform.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44's Starter plan costs $16/month when billed annually or $20/month when billed monthly. The plan includes monthly message and integration credits, with usage allowances affecting how much building and iteration can be completed within the plan.


Base44 suits builders who prioritize initial speed and are comfortable building within its managed app development environment.


## **5. Replit**


Replit provides a full cloud development environment with AI assistance through Replit Agent. Founded in 2016, it serves both educational and professional development use cases.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Full IDE environment** : Terminal access, package management, and complete development tools
- **Replit Agent** : AI-powered code generation within the IDE
- **Multi-language support** : Beyond TypeScript/React to Python, Node.js, and more
- **Collaboration features** : Tools for collaborative application development
- **Deployment included** : Hosting options for published applications


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit serves both non-technical builders using AI-assisted app creation and developers who want a full cloud IDE. It handles projects requiring custom configurations, specific packages, or languages beyond the typical app builder stack.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit Core costs $20/month on monthly billing, with Pro at $100/month for additional agent capacity and collaboration features. Replit uses effort-based billing for certain AI-assisted development activities, so usage beyond included plan allowances can increase monthly costs.


Replit supports natural-language app building for non-technical users while also offering terminal access and deeper code-level control for developers.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual app builder, founded in 2012. It offers deep visual workflow logic and an extensive plugin ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual workflow builder** : Drag-and-drop logic for complex business rules
- **Plugin marketplace** : Community-built integrations for extending app functionality
- **Built-in database** : Proprietary Bubble database for data storage
- **Responsive design** : Visual controls for mobile-responsive layouts
- **Agency ecosystem** : Network of Bubble developers for hire


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble handles complex SaaS applications with intricate workflows, multi-role permissions, and sophisticated business logic. It serves businesses building internal tools, marketplaces, and customer-facing applications.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble's Web Starter plan starts at $32/month when billed annually, with workload-based pricing that can increase costs as application usage grows. Native mobile publishing is available through separate Mobile and Web & Mobile plans.


The platform does not offer conventional source-code export, creating stronger platform dependency. Bubble suits organizations building complex applications that prefer visual development and are comfortable operating within its managed environment. Learning Bubble's workflow logic also requires time investment.


## **7. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow focuses on mobile-first development using the Flutter framework, offering Flutter-based applications for iOS and Android from a shared codebase.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Flutter-based** : Compiled mobile applications rather than conventional web wrappers
- **Visual builder** : Drag-and-drop interface for mobile UI
- **Code export** : Flutter/Dart source code download on eligible paid plans
- **Firebase integration** : Streamlined backend integration with Google Firebase
- **Custom code** : Ability to add custom Dart functions


### **App Building Considerations**


FlutterFlow targets builders prioritizing mobile app development who want Flutter output. It works well for mobile-first applications where web is secondary.


### **Organizational Fit**


FlutterFlow offers free prototyping, with its Basic plan starting at $39/month on monthly billing for features such as source-code download and app deployment. The focus on Flutter means a different technology stack than TypeScript/React alternatives.


FlutterFlow suits builders specifically targeting mobile platforms who are comfortable with the Flutter ecosystem or want to hand off to Flutter developers later.


## **8. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, edit, publish, and share websites and lightweight web applications directly inside ChatGPT. It offers a convenient workflow for people who already use ChatGPT and want to turn conversations into hosted applications.


### **Primary Focus**


- **ChatGPT-based building** : Create and refine websites and web apps through natural language prompts
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish projects and share them using hosted URLs
- **Persistent data** : Supports database storage and uploaded files
- **User authentication** : Supports ChatGPT-based sign-in and authenticated experiences
- **Custom domains** : Available where supported by plan and workspace settings


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites works well for interactive websites, internal dashboards, resource hubs, lightweight business applications, and tools that use connected data.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans, including Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise, with usage, storage, and publishing permissions depending on the account or workspace. Building and editing count toward Codex usage. Hosting is currently included with Plus and Pro, while hosting charges for Enterprise are currently waived. Usage and storage limits still apply.


ChatGPT Sites suits users who want to build and host lightweight web applications directly in ChatGPT. Floot provides another approach through its MCP connector, managed Postgres database, payment integrations, and iOS and Android publishing workflows.


## **Why Floot Fits Builders Who Need Managed Apps**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) helps non-technical founders, business owners, and teams build full-stack applications without manually configuring backend infrastructure. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations to create, edit, test, and publish applications, depending on connector permissions.


Floot's[managed backend services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) include PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, hosting, payments, and transactional email. Connector-driven development uses existing AI subscriptions, with daily building-action limits and separate hosting and AI-feature allowances. Users retain code and data ownership, with project ZIP downloads available on paid plans.


Floot supports[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) on every plan, with 2 monthly builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, while app-store publishing also requires the relevant developer accounts and store approval.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How does Floot's pricing compare to Emergent?**


Floot Pro costs $25/month on monthly billing with 1,000 daily building actions and 12 mobile builds per month, while Emergent Standard costs $20/month when billed annually with 100 monthly credits. The key difference is that connector-driven building on Floot uses existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions without a second Floot AI build-credit bill. Floot's paid plans also include separate AI-credit and hosting allowances, with hosting usage beyond included allowances deducted from prepaid hosting credits. Floot does not automatically charge a payment card for hosting unless auto-reload is enabled. Floot's daily-reset building actions and Emergent's monthly AI credits use different measurement systems, so their allowances are not directly comparable.


### **Can mobile apps be built with these Emergent alternatives?**


Mobile support varies significantly. Floot includes[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) on all plans through a native shell approach. Emergent offers React Native capabilities. Lovable builds mobile-friendly web apps, Bolt.new supports mobile projects through Expo, and Base44 offers mobile app packaging for app-store submission. FlutterFlow specializes in Flutter-based mobile applications. Replit supports mobile development through Expo integration. Bubble offers native mobile app development through its Mobile and Web & Mobile plans. App-store publishing requirements vary by platform, and Apple and Google developer accounts may still be required.


### **What happens if building actions or credits run out?**


Credit-based platforms like Emergent and Lovable offer different credit allowances, reset rules, and purchasing options. Floot's connector building-action limits reset daily, and failed actions do not count. Floot's separate AI credits apply to features such as image generation, AI inside applications, and its optional agent. Hosting is also usage-based, with[allowances and prepaid credits](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/hosting) used to cover application hosting costs.


### **Can code be exported and self-hosted later?**


Floot users own their code and data on every plan. The TypeScript/React project ZIP is available on paid plans, while the PostgreSQL database can be exported on any plan. Self-hosting requires additional migration work, including replacing Floot-managed services and moving uploaded files separately. See[Floot's self-hosting guide](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) for details. Lovable offers GitHub integration. Replit provides full code access. FlutterFlow exports Flutter/Dart code on eligible paid plans. Bubble does not offer conventional source-code export, creating stronger platform dependency. Export capabilities matter if anticipating the need to move to custom infrastructure later.


### **How long does it take to build a working app?**


Build time depends on complexity, and simple applications generally require less development and testing than projects with complex workflows.[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) can simplify the setup process for users already familiar with supported AI assistants, since application development can take place within an existing AI workflow. Floot also handles core infrastructure such as hosting, authentication, and database services. More complex applications with custom workflows, integrations, and mobile deployment often require additional development, testing, and publishing work regardless of platform choice.
